newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW-Endemol expects to restore confidence.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Endemol expects to restore confidence.

text.p: TV production firm Endemol NV said on Thursday it expected to restore deflated investor confidence in the company which has led to marked underperformance of its share price on the Amsterdam bourse.

CFO Aat Schouwenaar told Reuters in an interview that even though a 19 percent first-half profit rise reported on April 8 fell within Endemol's forecast of a 15-20 percent rise, market expectations had been pitched higher and were disappointed.

"Confidence was damaged but I'm convinced we will be able to restore that confidence in the coming months," he said as the company announced it would announce in the next few months the acquisition of a television production firm in a major European country.
About a third of Endemol's shares were floated on the Amsterdam bourse last October at 48 guilders each.

After peaking at over 63 guilders just before the first-half results, the shares have since slumped back to around the flotations price -- a drop of about 23 percent in a period when Amsterdam's AMX mid-cap index has risen 17 percent.
Schouwenaar said with the benefit of hindsight the company now realised it was partly to blame for not signalling to analysts before the results that their estimates were too high.

Schouwenaar said he and other Endemol executives were not too worried by the underperformance of the company's shares and believed the share price would recover, as long as Endemol delivered on last year's promise of sustained profit growth.
"We are staying with our forecast of profit growth of 15 to 20 percent this year...and our long-term vision of a doubling of turnover and profits in five years," he said.
Schouwenaar said the mere fact that Endemol had been left behind in the broader share market rally had made the shares look cheap and could in itself fuel a recovery.
